children: Succession planning is a task financial advisors know they should do, but many drag their feet. In addition to the time and effort involved, succession planning reminds them that their business, which many built from scratch, won't be theirs forever. They know they may eventually suffer a loss of identity, which can cause great stress and anxiety, says Scott Danner, the chief growth officer of Steward Partners, on Barron's Advisor's The Way Forward podcast.
"We have seen people sell their businesses and make tens of millions of dollars and look like they've lost their loved one," says Danner. "They've lost something in themselves."
In his current role at Steward, which ranked No. 9 on Barron's 2025 list of top RIA firms, Danner applies his expertise in M&A, succession planning, and business development.

One recent example: In June, Steward recruited Zelniker Dorfman Private Wealth, a $2.4 billion UBS breakaway team that serves athletes, entertainers, and other wealthy clients. Peter Dorfman, who leads the practice with Scott Zelniker, said at the time of the transaction they were increasingly attracted to Steward's employee-ownership model and hybrid RIA and brokerage services.

Danner built his own company, Freedom Street Partners, into a firm with nearly $3.5 billion in assets under advisement before selling it to Steward Partners in 2023 when he was 45. The emotional component was one reason he sold at that point, he says. "I wanted to do it early, not later in my career or my life," he says.
On the podcast, Danner emphasizes that successful business growth should include strategic partnerships, succession planning, and a balanced life. That includes making time for family.

"A lot of us advisors-I've heard this conversation-they say, 'Oh, everything I do is for my family,' yet they're never home and they miss every major event." He says of colleagues, "They're extremely driven. They're amazing humans, but work is a problem and it creates that burnout. And the burnout may not just be your burnout, it may be your family's burnout."
